title: Being a good friend
examples: What should I do if my friend is upset?
How do I show someone I care?
Is it always okay to share my toys?

explain.say: Today you will learn about being a good friend. Kindness means caring about other people.
Sharing means letting others use your things too. You can share your crayons.

draw.text: Sharing: Letting others use your things.

explain.say: Everyone makes mistakes. When you make a mistake, you can say sorry. Saying sorry helps make things better.

items: Step 2: Notice how your friend feels

explain.say: A good friend listens. Listening shows that you care.
When you play, take turns with the toys. First it is your turn, then your friend has a turn.
If a friend is sad, you can ask what would help. You can ask if they would like a hug.

faq.q: What if I do not want to share my favourite toy?
faq.a: It is okay to feel that way. You can say, can I have five more minutes, then you can have a turn?
asks: How do I ask to use something?

faq.q: What if my friend does not say sorry?
faq.a: You can tell a grown-up who is nearby. They can help you talk about it.
asks: Who do I tell if it is hard?
Can I make them say sorry?

faq.q: Is being kind only for big kids?
faq.a: No, being kind is for everyone, all the time. Little actions make big differences.
asks: Do I have to be perfect?

faq.q: What is the best way to show kindness?
faq.a: The best way is to notice when someone needs a smile or a helping hand. Small acts count the most.
asks: What is the kindest thing to do?
How often should I be kind?

faq.q: If I say sorry, do I have to do anything else?
faq.a: It is good to say sorry and then try to fix it with your actions. Actions show you mean it.

facts: Kindness means treating others with care and warmth.
Sharing means taking turns with toys or snacks.
When you make a mistake, saying sorry is important.
Good friends listen when others are speaking.

quiz.say: Your friend drops their books. What is a kind thing to do?
quiz.why: Helping shows your friend that you care.

wrong.0: Walking away leaves your friend to do it alone.
wrong.2: Laughing can make your friend feel sad or silly.

quiz.say: You have the crayon. Your friend wants it too. What can you do?
quiz.why: Taking turns means you both get to use the crayon.

wrong.1: Keeping it all day means your friend gets no turn.
wrong.2: Hiding it means nobody gets to use it.

quiz.say: You bump into your friend by accident. What can you say?
quiz.show: 💥 You bump your friend. What can you say?

options.show: I am sorry. Are you okay?
options.say: I am sorry. Are you okay?

quiz.why: Saying sorry shows you care how your friend feels.

wrong.0: Watch out tells your friend to take care, but you did the bump.
wrong.1: Blaming your friend can hurt their feelings, and the bump was an accident.
